task_context.reference_solution:
Converting to degrees,
\[-\frac{3 \pi}{4} = \frac{180^\circ}{\pi} \cdot \left( -\frac{3 \pi}{4} \right) = -135^\circ.\]Since the tangent function has period $180^\circ,$ $\tan (-135^\circ) = \tan (-135^\circ + 180^\circ) = \tan 45^\circ = \boxed{1}.$

That is a very productive line of thinking. The tangent function has a period of $\pi$ (or $180^\circ$), which means $\tan(\theta) = \tan(\theta + \pi)$. Applying that property to your angle should lead you directly to a value you likely already know from the unit circle.
